rationale: Masking personal identities in displayed data protects privacy and prevents disclosure.
Requires an encrypted channel for exchanging patient data, protecting it from disclosure; no alteration detection is mentioned.
Requires verification that detects records altered since saving, which is data integrity.
Anti-malware scanning and quarantine of malicious files is detecting and blocking malware.
Idle-timeout session end and lock explicitly aims to limit exploitation of an unattended session (rule 7).
Per-clinic encryption keys ensure one clinic cannot decrypt another's records, protecting data from unauthorized disclosure.
Restricts who may create, modify or cancel bookings to privileged staff, a modification-control requirement.
Limits applications to authorised screen regions and hides the rest, restricting access to visible content.
Account recovery requires the user to prove control of the registered email, a verification of identity.
Restricts write and delete permissions on production tables to explicitly privileged accounts.
Verifying the ownership mark of firmware and rejecting modified images detects alteration and checks the origin of the component.
Ensures every hub and app authenticates the user only with the current credential, which concerns identity verification.
Validates configuration values for type and range and aborts on failure, i.e. data validity checking, though no attacker or protection purpose is stated.
Only the physician role may amend diagnosis entries and other roles are rejected, restricting modification.
Limits each app to reading only the needed device states and conceals other sensor readings.
Detects manipulated booking reference, date or price via signature and cancels the reservation, protecting data integrity.
Enforces credential reset across all modules so identity checks use the latest credential.
Restricts edits of salary and bank records to roles with update rights.
Computing a cryptographic digest so later changes can be detected is alteration detection.
Requires valid credentials from the developer before accepting a build request.
Signature validation at launch blocks altered extensions and settings, detecting modification and verifying origin.
Rejects non-conforming values and keeps the stored row unmodified, enforcing data validity and integrity.
Per-customer encryption keys keep one customer's data unreadable to others.
Encrypted transport so eavesdroppers cannot read content protects against disclosure.
Requires detection of tampered historical data with bounded error so data accuracy can be trusted.
Sets a minimum strength for the PIN or passphrase used to authenticate the cardholder at activation.
Prevents other processes from modifying or deleting saved recordings.
Rejecting messages with duplicate nonce or sequence counter defends against replay attacks.
Restricts write access to sales figures to authorised analysts so unauthorised users cannot change them.
Requires detecting any alteration of the scenario file between release and loading.
Requires a unique identifier and pairing credential and confirmation of resident status before enrolment, i.e. identity verification.
Limits viewing of personal and business-critical tables and fields to explicitly permitted roles.
A MAC verified before display or processing detects alteration; origin verification is not stated.
A tamper-evident mark in statements allows any modification to be detected.
Returns only data the requesting account has permission to read, restricting read access.
The integrity mark must survive copying, compression and deliberate editing meant to erase it, covering tamper detection and resistance to deliberate attack.
Erasing memory holding payment details prevents later sessions from reading residual data.
Only a signed-in device administrator may modify enterprise policy settings, restricting who can modify.
Requires a registered account name and matching credential before accepting device commands, i.e. user authentication.
